concerns: Key inferences are labeled as indirect in the proposal; the available evidence provides guidance (MISEV2023) and rodent demonstration of therapeutic-relevance but does not experimentally validate the spike-in identity gate itself.

Driedonks et al. (macaque) shows intranasal biodistribution limitations and supports the proposal’s caution, but it does not contradict nor validate the spike-in assay—bridging experiments (including short-interval in vivo recovery) are required before treating a bounded fraction as clinically relevant EV drug-substance.

The proposal assumes capture-compatibility and buffer-insensitivity of immuno-capture reagents and particle counters; MISEV recommends orthogonal characterization but does not provide program-specific validation data—this creates risk of false negatives if not experimentally confirmed.

Detergent/protease protection can help indicate membrane-protected material, but no supplied evidence demonstrates that the chosen protease/detergent conditions reliably differentiate EVs from detergent-resistant non-vesicular contaminants in the program’s fractionation context.

Spike-in design, orthogonality (species/isotope), and lack of cross-reactivity are critical but not supported by the provided canonical evidence; poor spike-in performance would invalidate within-sample controls and the proposed gate.
conclusion: The proposal is broadly consistent with the cited canonical evidence (MISEV2023 guidance, rodent intranasal EV efficacy studies, and macaque intranasal biodistribution limitations) and is plausibly supported as an operational identity strategy, but key experimental demonstrations required to validate the spike-in–controlled, fraction-level qualitative gate are missing and pose material translational risk.
evidence_gap: No direct experimental evidence in the supplied canonical set that (a) an exogenous intact-EV spike-in added pre-fractionation reproducibly enables a per-lot, fraction-level qualitative pass/fail identity gate across >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots and (b) the proposed detergent/protease protection + capture co-localization readouts reliably distinguish bona fide membrane-protected EVs from co-eluting non-vesicular particles (e.g., lipoproteins/aggregates) in production-relevant material and across species/scale. Also missing is canonical evidence that capture reagents and buffer panels validated per MISEV produce consistent, interference-free readouts in the specific capture + particle-counter workflow envisioned.
